name: Ui_PagerWindow_InitPageNumbers
summary: Sets up the pager's six numbered text labels (null_txt_l0..l5 over txt_l0..l5) and the pager_num_r/pager_num_l counters, then rebuilds the page-id list from the owned items in the bag (work+0x24A98), sorts it by the item record's sort key (+0xB) and notifies the window.
evidence: Named callees Game_GetWork/Ui_PagerWindow_IntrosortU8/Game_GetDataManager now pin the function: the id source is the bag at work+0x24A98 (established fact), so the sorted list is the pager's item pages, not a generic table walk. Six-iteration digit loop and the two pager labels are unchanged from the first pass.

name: Ui_CursorWindow_Init
summary: Initialises a small cursor widget: runs the shared UI base ctor, asks the widget for its animation id (vtable slot 0x5C) and attaches that animation through Ui_PlayAnimByName on the widget's anim owner (self[1]), storing the handle at self+0x4C.
evidence: Both BL callers are named: Casino_PokerWindow_SetActiveCards (0x004DC768) and 0x004DC260 initialise the two embedded cursor windows at +0x4C/+0x9C with this function and then set the card digits. The body's only work is drN + Ui_PlayAnimByName, i.e. cursor-widget animation setup.

name: Ui_FourRowIconWindow_InitPanes
summary: Pane initialiser of a four-row window: generates txt_l1../null_txt_l1.. four times, stores the fixed slot-byte pattern at +0x49..+0x4B (0xFF/1/0xFF or 0/1/2 depending on Ui_IsMode(3)) and refreshes the four icon layers from the table at 0x007A9958.
evidence: The four-iteration loop (bound 4), the 'null_txt_l1' literal and Ui_TextLayer_SetText calls match the name; vtable 0x0076BAC8 slot +7 and the Ui_FourRowIconWindow_Ctor at 0x003F1D08 name this class as the InitPanes virtual.

name: Ui_Widget_BindAnimFromCommand
summary: Binds one animation to a UI widget: takes the widget's text-command record, resolves the named animation through func_0062AB3C on the game work, attaches the animation pane descriptor (0x00747874) with vtable+0x34 and installs the animation data with func_001A6210; falls back to a default animated object when the command carries no name.
evidence: Callees are now named: maybe_Text_FindMessageCommand (the command record), Os_GetGameWork and the animation install func_001A6210. That makes the previous 'SetupWidgetAnimation' correct in substance but vague about the source, so the name now says the animation comes from the text command record.

name: Ui_Balloon_BindParts
summary: Binds a speech balloon's layout: attaches the four panes from the static table at 0x007A89A4 via vtable+0x34 and then binds the two balloon text parts at self+0x13 (part 0) and self+0xE5 (part 1) with Ui_Balloon_BindWinParts.
evidence: The callee is now the named Ui_Balloon_BindWinParts, called twice with part indices 0 and 1 on the two embedded text-part blocks - so this is a balloon, not a generic four-part widget; the four table entries are just the balloon's panes.

name: Ui_TextLayerWindow_Init
signature: void Ui_TextLayerWindow_Init(UiWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Window initialiser whose whole job is to give the dual-layer text renderer embedded at self+0x70 its default setup (Text_SetupDualLayersDefault), after the shared UI base constructor.
evidence: The callee is now named Text_SetupDualLayersDefault, and the sibling Ui_TextLayerWindow_SetupDualLayers (0x0066D294) names the class; the vtable 0x00766C30 slot +8 is the window init slot used by every class in this neighbourhood.

name: Ui_SevenSlotWindow_InitPanes
summary: Pane initialiser of a seven-row window: generates txt_l1../null_txt_l1.. for seven rows, records the slot bytes +0x49..+0x4F (0,0,1,2,3,4,5) and refreshes the seven icon layers with Ui_TextLayer_SetText.
evidence: Seven iterations confirmed in the readable body (loop ends when 6 < index) plus the 'null_txt_l1' literal; Ui_SevenSlotWindow_Ctor (0x003F1284) names this class and points at this function as its slot +7 initialiser.

name: Ui_DigitRowWidget_Init
summary: Initialises a four-row numeric text widget: generates four numbered rows with the null_txt_l1 overlay template, then binds text id 1 to the static default glyph string at 0x007AA1A4 and clears the row-state byte at +0x49.
evidence: The four-iteration digit loop and the null_txt_l1 template are confirmed in the body, and the named Ui_TextLayer_SetText call shows the final write is a text-layer default, not an event hook as the first pass guessed.

name: maybe_Ui_SetOwnerAndDispatch
summary: Stores the owner/layout word (arg->f_AC) at self+0x70, points self+0x6C at self and dispatches through self->f_4C->f_18. The decompiler lost the jumptable at 0x0018F310, so the real body is larger than what is visible and the release/finalise reading is unproven.
evidence: Re-read with the neighbours: the visible code wires an owner pointer and jumps through a child vtable - that is attach/init behaviour, not the 'release the child list' the first pass assumed (no free, no list walk). The name is changed to describe only what is visible; the tail is lost to a bad jumptable, so confidence stays low.

name: Ui_LayoutChild_InitDispatch
summary: Chooses one of the two embedded layout children (self+0x4C or self+0xD18 by self->f_49), stores the parent and the layout word at child[8]/child[9] and dispatches the child's init virtual (slot +0x18).
evidence: Body verified line by line against the readable C: the two child blocks, the f_49 selector and the owner/layout stores are all visible; only the child class name remains unknown, which this name does not claim.

name: maybe_Ui_UnknownPaneSetupC
summary: Unrecoverable vtable-slot-7 pane setup: only the shared UI layout prologue (drN) exists before halt_baddata at 0x002C4950. Nothing about the panes it would create survives in the decompiler output.
evidence: No new named callers or callees; the disassembly really does stop at a bad instruction, so the function stays unnamed by design.

name: Ui_TwoTextWindow_InitPanesB
summary: Attaches the two text rows 'txt_l1' and 'txt_l2' (ids 0 and 1) to the window and then is lost to a bad instruction at 0x00323F68; further panes, if any, are not recoverable.
evidence: The two string literals resolve to 'txt_l1'/'txt_l2' (0x00324214/0x0032421C) and the vtable 0x00763BA4 slot +7 marks this as an InitPanes override, matching the name; the truncation is stated in the summary rather than papered over.

name: Ui_TwoListWindow_Init
summary: Window initialiser that adopts the two embedded list widgets at self+0x80 and self+0xD8: stores both pointers at f_130/f_134 and, for each, calls virtual +8 to attach the owner and +0xC to reset the list.
evidence: The twice-repeated attach(+8)/reset(+0xC) pair on the two embedded widgets is fully visible in the body and the vtable 0x00763E68 slot +8 is the window init slot; the class has no pane strings, so 'two list widgets' is as specific as the evidence goes.

name: Ui_NumberedTextRowsWindow_InitPanes
summary: Creates three numbered text rows from the 'null_txt_l1' template, advancing the digit each iteration and registering each row through virtual +0x34 and +0x38, then finishes the layout with +0x48.
evidence: Three-iteration bound and the null_txt_l1 literal (0x0032BC9C) are confirmed in the body; vtable 0x00764100 slot +7 and the identical construction in 0x0039335C support the generic 'numbered text rows window' reading.

name: Ui_TitleTextWindow_InitPanes
summary: Attaches the 'txt_title' pane and a second one-character 'txt' pane to the window at the base layout id.
evidence: Both literals resolve in the retail image: 0x0032E604 = 'txt_title' and 0x0032E610 = 'txt'. With vtable 0x007644D4 slot +7 this is exactly a two-pane title window initialiser.

name: maybe_Ui_FiveChildWindow_Init
summary: Window initialiser that stores five embedded sub-widget pointers (at +0x384..+0x398) and, for each, attaches the owner via virtual +8 and resets it via +0xC; nothing identifies what the five widgets display.
evidence: The body shows five attach/reset pairs, but no pane names and no named callee reveal whether they are lists; 'FiveListWindow' over-claimed, so the name now says only that there are five children.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipmentListWindow_InitPanes_2
signature: void maybe_Ui_EquipmentListWindow_InitPanes_2(UiWindow* self, UiLayout* layout, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Builds a paged list whose rows have four columns - index (txt_lN), name (txt_eN), number (txt_numN) and right-hand value (txt_rN) - plus pager_num_r/pager_num_l and a digit-incrementing row generator.
evidence: The string resolver confirms the four column families ('txt_e1', 'txt_num1', 'txt_r1', 'null_txt_l0' at 0x00365754..0x00365798) and the two pager labels, so the column layout is certain; whether 'e' means equipment or effect still is not.

name: Ui_NumberedTextRowsWindow_InitPanesB
summary: Variant of the three-row numbered text window: builds three rows from 'null_txt_l1' with an incrementing digit, registering each through virtual +0x34/+0x38 and finishing with +0x48.
evidence: Same verified three-row construction and the same null_txt_l1 literal as 0x0032BB2C, but its own vtable (0x00766D30 slot +7), so it is a sibling class rather than the same one.

name: Ui_ThreeRowNullTextWindow_InitPanes
summary: Reserves three text slots: binds the null overlays 'null_txt_l1', 'null_txt_l2' and 'null_txt_l3' at row ids 0..2 and finishes the layout; no visible labels are created.
evidence: All three literals (0x003B5768/74/80) resolve and the body has no visible-row calls, which matches the 'null text' name exactly.

name: Ui_ThreeRowNullTextWindow_InitPanesB
summary: Second three-null-row window: binds 'null_txt_l1..l3' at row ids 0..2 and then is cut off by a bad jumptable at 0x003C2450.
evidence: The three literals (0x003C2454/60/6C) resolve and the calls are visible; the truncation after the third row is noted, but the three-row null-pane role is proven.

name: maybe_Ui_SingleTextPaneWindow_Init
summary: Minimal window initialiser: base ctor, then exactly one text pane named 'txt' at the base layout id and nothing else.
evidence: The undecoded literal at 0x003D6278 resolves to 'txt' in the retail image, so the first pass's 'unnamed pane' caveat is gone; the pane content ('txt') is still too generic to say which screen this window belongs to.

name: Ui_TwelveRowNumberedTextWindow_InitPanes
summary: Creates twelve numbered text rows from the 'null_txt_l1' template (two-digit suffix increment), each with its null overlay, and finishes the layout.
evidence: Twelve-iteration bound confirmed in the body and the null_txt_l1 literal (0x003D6AF8) resolves; vtable 0x0076A3B0 slot +7 identifies the InitPanes override.

name: Ui_ThreeRowNumberedTextWindow_InitPanes
summary: Creates three null-text overlay rows ('null_txt_l1' with an incremented digit), with no visible labels, and finishes the layout.
evidence: Three-iteration loop and the null_txt_l1 literal (0x003D6BFC) are visible; the name now states that only null overlays are bound, which the body confirms.

name: maybe_Ui_TxtLWindow_Init
summary: Minimal window initialiser that binds a single text pane whose name literal at 0x003E9FD8 is 'txt_l' (an unterminated-prefix name, not a numbered row).
evidence: The previously undecoded literal resolves to 'txt_l' in the retail image, so the pane name is now known; a single 'txt_l' pane still does not identify the screen, hence maybe_.

name: Ui_TxtRightWindow_InitPanes
summary: Smallest pane initialiser: base ctor plus one right-aligned text pane 'txt_r' at the window's base layout id.
evidence: The literal at 0x003EB560 resolves to 'txt_r' and the body contains no other pane call; vtable 0x0076B774 slot +0x34 is the pane-setup slot of its class.

name: Ui_SevenLineTextWindow_InitPanes
summary: Pane initialiser of a seven-line text window: attaches txt_1..txt_7 plus a right-aligned txt_r, then anchors the four arrow panes txt_4..txt_7 to the 'null_arrow' reference pane using the centre of the txt_3/txt_4 block as origin.
evidence: Every literal resolves in the retail image ('txt_1'..'txt_7', 'txt_r', 'null_arrow' at 0x003F7524..0x003F7564), and the four-entry static table at 0x007290F8 pairs arrow ids 3..6 with those panes; the name now states the arrow anchoring instead of only 'seven lines'.

name: Ui_NameStatWindow_InitPanes
summary: Character panel initialiser: one txt_name header, three left stat labels (txt_l1..l3) and three right value labels (txt_r1..r3), each with its null_ overlay, then a refresh; the text formats are the S/M/H/I/F/P style blobs at 0x004020BC..
evidence: All fourteen literals resolve (txt_name, txt_l1..l3, txt_r1..r3, null_txt_l1..l3, null_txt_r1..r3) and the format blobs decode to the 'S0F0R0M0'/'h0O0N0'/'i0F0P0' style strings, so the name/stat split is confirmed, not guessed.

name: Ui_FourLineMenuWindow_InitPanes
summary: Four-row menu initialiser: binds txt_l1..txt_l4 plus their null_txt_l1..l4 overlays with style 0x15 and refreshes the layout.
evidence: All eight literals resolve and the null overlays are bound with style 0x15; vtable 0x0076C800 slot +0x34 is the pane-setup slot. The style constant is the only thing distinguishing this class from 0x00402DC8.

name: Ui_FourLineMenuWindow_InitPanesB
summary: Second four-row menu initialiser: same txt_l1..txt_l4 rows and null_txt_l1..l4 overlays, but the overlays use null style 9 instead of 0x15, i.e. a differently styled sibling class.
evidence: The call sequence is identical to 0x004026E4 apart from the style constant (9 vs 0x15) and the class vtable (0x0076C89C vs 0x0076C800), which the readable C shows directly; the name keeps the B suffix to mark the sibling.

name: Ui_TwoLineTextWindow_InitPanes
summary: Two-line text window initialiser: attaches txt_l1 and txt_l2 (the second with text format blob 0x00403148) and their null overlays with styles 0x14 and 0x16, then refreshes.
evidence: All literals resolve and the two distinct null styles are visible in the body, so the two-line reading is exact; vtable 0x0076CA38 slot +0x34 is the pane-setup slot.

name: Ui_SixPairMenuWindow_InitPanes
summary: Two-column menu initialiser: right-hand rows txt_r1..txt_r6 first, then left-hand rows txt_l1..txt_l6, followed by six null_txt_l1..l6 overlays with style 9 and a refresh.
evidence: All eighteen literals resolve and the fill order (right column, then left) is visible; vtable 0x0076CB6C slot +0x34 confirms the pane-setup role.

name: maybe_Ui_PagedTextChildWindow_InitPanes
signature: void maybe_Ui_PagedTextChildWindow_InitPanes(UiPopupWindow* self, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4, int arg5)
summary: InitPanes override that only forwards to the paged-text row initialiser on the embedded child at self+0x70; no panes of its own are created.
evidence: The callee is now known to be the five-row paged text initialiser (0x0041DD7C), so this window is a thin container around a paged text child; nothing in the body identifies it as a popup, which the old name assumed.

name: maybe_Ui_FourPairTextWindow_InitPanes
summary: Four-plus-four row window: binds the four right-hand rows txt_r1..txt_r4 first and then the four left-hand rows txt_l1..txt_l4 at successive layout ids 0..7.
evidence: All eight literals resolve (0x00405220..0x00405258) and the body binds exactly those eight panes with no pager or overlays, so 'four left + four right' is proven; 'ShopWindow' was an invention from the neighbouring swap window and is dropped.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipmentListWindow_InitPanes
summary: Large scrollable list initialiser: three digit-incrementing loops attach 28 indexed rows (txt_l0..) with matching null overlays, then the pager_num_r/pager_num_l labels and a txt_title_l header.
evidence: The literals confirm 28 generated rows plus the two pager labels and 'txt_title_l'; the class is still identified only by sharing the equipment window's pager labels, so the equipment attribution stays a hypothesis.

name: Ui_RotatePaneWindow_Init
signature: void Ui_RotatePaneWindow_Init(UiWindow* self, UiLayout* layout, u32 unusedA, u32 unusedB, u32 unusedC)
summary: Binds the 'null_rot' pane, stores it at self+0x4C and gives it a symmetric rotation (the same angle on both axes) plus a source position from the window's f_50, setting bit 0x10 in the pane attribute byte.
evidence: The 'null_rot' literal resolves (0x004468D8) and the body writes pane->f_1C = pane->f_24 = the angle constant and pane->f_20 = f_50 - a rotation pane, exactly as the name says.

name: Ui_ThreePairNumberWindow_InitPanes
summary: Number-cell initialiser: six iterations cover three rows times two columns, and each cell binds four panes named txt_{l|r}N_num1, _num1_1, _num1_2 and _num1_3 (24 panes in total).
evidence: The body's six-iteration loop with l/r selection (0x6C/0x72) and suffix patches 1/2/3 is fully readable; the first pass counted twelve panes, the real count is 24, which the summary now states.

name: Ui_ThreeModePaneWindow_InitPanes
summary: Window owning three independent ten-pane mode groups: initialises the sub-windows at +0x14, +0xE0 and +0x1AC with modes 1, 2 and 3, then binds the three null_txt_l1..l3 overlays.
evidence: The named callee maybe_Ui_TenRowModePanes_Setup is called three times with mode bytes 1/2/3, and the three null literals resolve (0x0045E7E8/7F4/800); the mode grouping is proven, not inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init
summary: Minimal window initialiser that binds the single text pane 'txt' at the window's base layout id.
evidence: The undecoded literal at 0x004AAD00 resolves to 'txt', so the pane name is now known; a lone 'txt' pane still does not identify the screen, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init_776168
summary: Window initialiser of class (vtable 0x00776168) that binds the single text pane 'txt'; Ghidra stops at a jumptable right after the call (the 0x004ADCFC argument is a code address, not data), so any further panes are unrecovered.
evidence: The literal at 0x004ADD00 resolves to 'txt' and the 4th argument 0x004ADCFC is inside the function's own code range, which shows the decompiler truncated rather than that the function is empty. The class stays identified by its vtable address.

name: maybe_Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init_776E00
summary: Window initialiser of class (vtable 0x00776E00) that binds the single text pane 'txt'; the tail after the call is lost to a jumptable.
evidence: The literal at 0x004B741C resolves to 'txt', so the previously 'no panes' description was wrong - it binds exactly one text pane. The class is still only identifiable by its vtable address.

name: maybe_Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init_778C24
summary: Window initialiser of class (vtable 0x00778C24) that binds the single text pane 'txt' before the decompiler loses the jumptable tail.
evidence: The undecoded literal at 0x004CF83C resolves to 'txt'; the body is the same one-pane shape as 0x004AACC0, so the name now says what is actually bound.

name: Ui_TwoLineTextWindow2_Init
summary: Two-line numbered text widget: binds txt_l1/txt_l2 with their null_txt overlays, seeds a four-byte digit buffer (0x30503055 = full-width '01') and applies the text-format blob at 0x004D3DB4.
evidence: All literals resolve (txt_l1, txt_l2, null_txt_l1, null_txt_l2, format blob at 0x004D3DB4), so the two-line structure is proven; the '2' suffix still only distinguishes it from the other two-line window class.

name: maybe_Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init_77A4BC
summary: Window initialiser of class (vtable 0x0077A4BC) that binds the single text pane 'txt'.
evidence: The literal at 0x004DCECC resolves to 'txt', replacing the first pass's 'no panes' claim; the class remains identified only by its vtable address.

name: maybe_Ui_TextPaneWindow_Init_77B64C
summary: Window initialiser of class (vtable 0x0077B64C) that binds the single text pane 'txt'.
evidence: The literal at 0x004E74EC resolves to 'txt', so this is a one-pane text window rather than the empty widget the first pass described.

name: Ui_TxtL1Window_Init
summary: Minimal window initialiser that binds one text pane named 'txt_l1' at the base layout id.
evidence: The literal at 0x004EE878 resolves to 'txt_l1' (the first pass could only repeat the header's claim); a window with just that one row is precisely described by the new name.

name: Ui_ClockWindow_InitPanes
summary: Clock/date readout initialiser: binds txt_l1, txt_r2, the three digit rows txt_r3_1..txt_r3_3 and the glyph panes txt_r3_period, txt_r3_colon1 and txt_r3_colon2, storing the three glyphs at self+0x4C..0x54.
evidence: All eight literals resolve (0x004FB124..0x004FB178), which confirms the clock reading (three digits plus period and two colons) far beyond the first pass's 'looks like a clock'.

name: Ui_TitlePagerWindow_InitPanes
summary: Initialises a titled paged window: binds the txt_title header and the two pager counters pager_num_r and pager_num_l.
evidence: All three literals resolve (0x004FBFEC/FF8/004FC004) and the body binds exactly those panes; this is the plainest example of the title+pager pattern, so confidence is at the top of the allowed range.

name: Ui_ModeListWindow_InitPanes
summary: Initialises a mode list: sets up the ten-row mode panes on the child at self+0x14 with mode 1 and binds one null_txt_l1 cursor row before finishing the layout.
evidence: The named callee maybe_Ui_TenRowModePanes_Setup plus the null_txt_l1 literal and the +0x48 finish call make this the same one-mode variant of the three-mode window at 0x0045E710.

name: Ui_Window_CreateBlackPane
signature: void Ui_Window_CreateBlackPane(UiWindow* self, UiWindowData* data, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Creates the window's full-screen backdrop by asking the layout object (data->f_AC->f_10) for the pane named 'black', stores it at self+0x90 and clears bit 0 of the pane's +0x44 flags so it starts hidden.
evidence: The pane-name literal at 0x0061A448 resolves to 'black', which makes the name exact; the body is only drN + one pane factory call + a flag clear.

name: maybe_Ui_PagedTextWindow_InitRowsBase
signature: void maybe_Ui_PagedTextWindow_InitRowsBase(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Initialiser of a window that first builds its base sub-object at self-0x70 and then hands the whole layout to the five-row paged-text initialiser (0x0041DD7C). The vtable slot is an init, not a destructor.
evidence: The callee is now known to be the paged-text row initialiser (0x0041DD7C) and the vtable at 0x0076CD54 holds it in an init slot next to Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub/Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim, so the first pass's 'destructor thunk' reading is wrong; the exact window class is still unidentified.

name: Ui_MenuCondition_Evaluate
summary: Evaluates one menu/command condition record (taken from the table via func_0063D338) and returns whether it holds: kind 0/4 = required items owned/needed, 3/8 = compare against the flag byte array at work+0x27508, 5 = equipped item stat compare over the six slots, 6 = party-member stat threshold.
evidence: The body is a switch on the record's kind byte (+8) whose branches call the now-named Item_LookupRecord, func_006292F0 (equipped item id) and func_0035EB98 (party-member record); the first pass's 'positions list rows' reading is therefore wrong - it evaluates conditions, it does not lay anything out.

name: Field_SceneObject_UpdateBalloon
summary: Re-places a field object's balloon billboard: resolves the balloon entry for the object id through the named Field_FindNpcBalloonEntry, scales the object's balloon size by 0.3/0.5/1.0 depending on its balloon mode byte (+0x313), places it at the object position and then shifts the child nodes by +/-0.8 in Y when the visible state changed.
evidence: The decisive callee is now named: Field_FindNpcBalloonEntry (entry type byte +1, party mask +2) is what gets positioned here, not a shadow definition - so 'UpdateShadow' was the wrong object, the billboard is the speech/emotion balloon.

name: Field_Object_ApplySpawnRecord
signature: void Field_Object_ApplySpawnRecord(FieldObject* self, int* rec, int arg3)
summary: Applies a spawn record to an existing field object: copies position, rotation, model ids and the mode byte (+0x313), rebuilds the rotation, updates the follow point, creates the sprite via Field_Actor_CreateSprite, optionally creates the billboard (Field_Actor_CreateBillboard) and finishes by playing the actor sound for the mode.
evidence: The callers are named (Field_SceneObject_SpawnFromRecord, Model_Equip_UpdateActorEquipment) and the callees are named (Gfx_Node_SetEulerRotation, Field_Actor_CreateSprite, Field_Actor_CreateBillboard, maybe_Field_CreateActorSound), so this is an apply-record routine; 'WithEffect' overstated the optional billboard branch, which the record byte +0x1F gates.

name: Field_Object_ReleaseSpriteResource
summary: Releases the object's sprite/model resource: if the packed handle at +0x370 is still registered in the global handle table and the manager exists, calls manager vtable+0x40 with category 4 and then clears the object's model through Field_SpawnObject_ApplyRecord(self, 0).
evidence: Named callee Field_SpawnObject_ApplyRecord plus the named caller maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_ReleaseByClass (class 0x007C4D9C) show this is a field-object resource release, not a map unlink; +0x40 vs +0x3C with the manager byte (the sibling 0x00183918) is the only difference between the two release categories.

name: maybe_Field_UpdateLocationGrid
summary: Re-registers a field actor in the shared spatial grid: calls func_005E78CC, re-applies the placement record when the manager flag +0x51 is clear, looks the actor's cell up by position (+0x258) and releases it if missing, then sets the actor state to 6.
evidence: The grid helpers (0x6282D0/0x17C8C4) and the 0x98-byte grid context (vtable 0x782A08) are still unnamed, so the grid reading rests on shape only; the new detail is that a failed lookup releases rather than inserts, and that the record re-apply is conditional on the manager byte.

name: maybe_Field_Object_ReleaseSpriteResourceB
summary: Second sprite/model release path: same packed-handle test, but calls manager vtable+0x3C with category 4 and then applies the manager's byte at +0x88 through Field_SpawnObject_ApplyRecord.
evidence: Its caller is the named maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_ReleaseByClassB, so the two functions are the two release categories for field objects; which category maps to which sprite class is still unknown, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Scene_AbortIfPointInBoxSet
summary: Copies the 0x60-byte oriented-box set descriptor from scene+0x38C and returns early from the caller as soon as the given point lies inside one of the boxes; it returns nothing and collects nothing.
evidence: The visible body only early-returns on the first containing box (there is no output buffer or count), so the first pass's 'collects points' reading was wrong; the caller Event_Rura_Start ignores any result, so the purpose of the gate is still unclear.

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateFollowPosition
summary: Computes a follow position/rotation for a field object: with a rail table at +0x314 it copies the current rail point's position and rotation (+0x334..+0x33C), otherwise it probes up to ten offsets around the target (random jitter, sin/cos, collision query 0x2E7F08) and keeps the first clear spot (+0x328..+0x330).
evidence: Re-read with the named callers: Field_Object_ApplySpawnRecord and the actor update code call it with a field object, not a camera, so 'camera' names the wrong owner - the fields written (+0x328..+0x33C) live in the object. The geometric probe itself is unchanged.

name: Field_ObjectSprite_CreateActor
summary: Creates the sprite actor for a field object: skipped while the UI overlay is active (overlay manager mode byte +0x281 == 1), otherwise resolves the object's kind-6 record, builds the quaternion and submits the sprite to the scene object manager (work+0x24A98); when the scene mode is 2 it also creates the child actors.
evidence: Named callees Field_Object_GetKind6Record and maybe_Field_ObjectSprite_CreateChildActors plus the UI-overlay guard at work+0x48/+0x281 (established offsets) confirm the sprite-actor creation role; the body returns 1/0 as 'created/skipped'.

name: maybe_Field_MapObject2D_SetupFromList19D4
summary: Initialises a 0x2C4-byte Field_MapObject2D from a record of the scene's f_19D4 object list: copies position, half-scaled rotation and quaternion into its sprite, sets the type id at +0x3C and the flags +0x64=1, +0x65=0, +0x66=rec+0x31.
evidence: The caller Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable is named and shows which list feeds this variant: f_19D0/f_19D4. The A/B/C/D suffix only distinguished siblings by accident, so the name now records the source list.

name: maybe_Field_MapObject2D_SetupFromList1A34
summary: Initialises a Field_MapObject2D from a record of the scene's f_1A34 object list: same sprite/transform setup as the 0x19D4 variant but leaves +0x3C untouched and stores +0x64=0, +0x65=0, +0x66=rec+0x31.
evidence: Caller Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable reads f_1A30/f_1A34 for this branch, which is what distinguishes it from its three siblings; the flag differences are visible in the readable C.

name: maybe_Field_MapObject2D_SetupFromList1B54
summary: Initialises a Field_MapObject2D from a record of the scene's f_1B54 object list: keeps the type-id copy to +0x3C but sets +0x64=1 and +0x65=1 and does not copy the record flag into +0x66.
evidence: The caller Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable reads f_1B50/f_1B54 for this branch; the flag pattern (+0x64=1, +0x65=1, no +0x66 copy) is visible in the body.

name: maybe_Field_MapObject2D_SetupFromList1BE4
summary: Initialises a Field_MapObject2D from a record of the scene's f_1BE4 object list: copies the type id to +0x3C, sets +0x64=0 and +0x65=1 and skips the record-flag copy.
evidence: The caller Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable reads f_1BE0/f_1BE4 for this branch; this is the fourth of the four per-list variants of the same constructor plus setup.

name: Field_Actor_ApplyPlacement
summary: Applies a full placement record to a model actor: writes the id byte (+0x220), position, scale (+0x88), builds the quaternion from the record's Euler angles and rebuilds the whole transform matrix/direction block from it.
evidence: The body copies exactly the placement layout (position at rec+8, angles at rec+0x14, scale at rec+0x20) into the actor transform fields and recomputes them with the named Math_BuildQuaternionFromEuler; caller Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable treats it as the per-record placement step.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_SyncAttachedNodes
summary: Per-frame positioner for the 2D nodes/light attached to an object: computes the owner transform (or rotates the local offset by the owner quaternion when +0x16A is set), writes the node position only when it actually changed, and repeats for every child node (type 1 position, type 2 position plus quaternion).
evidence: The quaternion helpers (0x574548/0x5744DC) and the child accessors (0x2E685C/0x2E5DA8) are still unnamed and the function is vtable-only, so the 'attached nodes' reading remains structural; the epsilon comparison is the only constant.

name: Actor_Action_Climb_Start
summary: Start step of the ladder/rope climb action: picks Ladder_Up_Start / Rope_Up_Start (and the down variants by the owner's step index), builds the orientation quaternion from Euler angles and snaps the hand node to the owner's rung offset.
evidence: All four animation names resolve as inline strings (Ladder_Up_Start, Ladder_Down_Start, Rope_Up_Start, Rope_Down_Start at 0x004F212C..0x004F2160), which pins the climb action and the kind/step branch that selects the clip.

name: Field_Scene_IsPointInsideBoxSetA
summary: Returns true when the given world point lies inside any type-1 oriented box of the scene's object set at +0x5AC (count +0x5B0): transforms the point into each box's frame and compares it with the half-extents plus epsilon.
evidence: The caller Field_DragonJumpAction_Update is named and uses the result as a landing check; the filter func_0062F0B4(work, type)==1 and the half-extent/epsilon comparison are visible. The 'A' suffix only separates it from the sibling set at +0x60C.

name: maybe_Field_Scene_IsPointOutsideBoxSet
summary: Same oriented-box test over the scene set at +0x60C (count +0x610, types +0x624), but returns the negated result: 1 when no box contains the point.
evidence: The body ends with 'result = uVar9 ^ 1' where uVar9 is set to 1 on containment, so the first pass's 'IsPointInside' name described the opposite of what it returns; the caller 0x00635ED4 is still unnamed.

name: Script_ParseBitwiseAnd
summary: Bitwise-AND level of the Squirrel compiler: parses the higher-precedence equality level (Script_SqCompiler_EqExp) and, while the next token is '&', pushes opcode 0x12 with sub-op 0.
evidence: Named callees Script_SqCompiler_EqExp, Sq_LexerReadToken, Script_ObjectVector_Pop/Script_IntVector_Push and maybe_Script_Compiler_PushStackOp make the parse-and-emit loop certain; the same body shape appears as the first loop of 0x001869C4.

name: Script_ParseBitwiseAndXor
summary: Bitwise-AND/OR-expression level of the Squirrel compiler: two loops, one consuming '&' and one consuming '^', each parsing an operand through the compiler's operator table and pushing opcode 0x12 with sub-op 0/3.
evidence: The body contains both loops (0x26 and 0x5E), so the first pass's XOR-only name was too narrow; the compiler-table indirect calls explain why no named caller shows up.

name: Party_Member_ApplyInventoryRecord
signature: void Party_Member_ApplyInventoryRecord(void* member, const u8* args)
summary: Fills a party member's 24 u16 inventory slots (+0xEC) from a party record: computes the page count through the text layout, saves and restores the layout state, blanks the six equipment slots (+0x11C), then copies each supplied item id into the next inventory slot - clearing the text cell of a slot first when func_006292A4 reports it as equipped - and finally refreshes the member's text page.
evidence: The caller SQCommand (0x0015179C) resolves the member with func_0035EB98 and compacts the equipment first; the body then writes the established member-inventory array at +0xEC and clears the six equipment bytes at +0x11C, so this is a party-inventory setup, not a 'text page build'.

name: maybe_Party_Member_CompactInventory
signature: void maybe_Party_Member_CompactInventory(void* member, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Rewrites a party member's 24-slot inventory after an equipment change: walks the non-empty prefix, removes entries whose slot does not report as equipped (memmove left, last slot set to 0xFFFF) and blanks the equipped ones with a text-cell clear, then notifies the item table (work+0x24ACC) for every removed id.
evidence: The loop runs over the established 24-slot inventory at member+0xEC (not over the six equipment bytes at +0x11C that the old name implied) and uses func_006292A4 as the equipped test; why both branches end up removing the entry is still unexplained, so maybe_ stays.

name: Party_ValidateEquipmentNames
signature: void Party_ValidateEquipmentNames(Actor* self, int command, int arg3)
summary: Re-applies every party member's font record and, when the equipment-change command 0x211 arrives with a non-zero flag, additionally revalidates all six equipment slots of all 31 members: for each slot it looks up the item record of the equipped id and clears/refreshes the member's name cells when the record changed.
evidence: The body is the same member loop as Party_ApplyFontsOnCommand plus a six-slot validation loop that uses Item_LookupRecord and the established equipment-slot array at +0x11C; nothing recalculates stats, so the old 'RecalcEquipment' was misleading.

name: Item_RemoveFromParty
signature: int Item_RemoveFromParty(void* work, u32 itemId, int maxCount, int skipSlots)
summary: Removes up to maxCount copies of item id from the party: the '%'-kind item (record +0xC == 0x25) is taken from the global counter at work+0x27C7C, bag items are decremented through the count table at work+0x24ACC, and otherwise the member inventories are scanned and the id is deleted from the first free slots, skipping the six equipped slots; returns how many were removed.
evidence: Decisive new evidence is the named caller AutoRemoveItemInParty (0x0015B938), which guards with `arg1 < 0xB3B` (the item-id range from the established facts) and calls this with (work, itemId, count, 0); the body then deletes the id from the member inventories and returns the count. The first pass's 'replace a character in names' reading was completely wrong.

name: Party_Member_ClearEquipSlots
summary: Blanks a party member's six equipment-slot bytes at +0x11C (all set to 0xFF) and refreshes the member's text cells and font record.
evidence: The six-byte loop starts at member+0x11C, the established equipment-slot array, on a member record (the same object Party_Member_ApplyInventoryRecord edits); the 'Ui_' prefix of the old name implied a screen object, which this is not.

name: Party_ApplyFontsOnCommand
signature: void Party_ApplyFontsOnCommand(void* self, u32 arg2, int command)
summary: When the party command id is 9, walks every active party member (count at work+0x27218, index via func_0066B0E4 on the bag) and re-applies the member's font/name record when the member's data-table entry has bit 1 set.
evidence: The only work in the loop is the named Text_ApplyFontRecord(member+4); there is no stat arithmetic anywhere, so 'RecalculateAllStats' described the wrong effect. The command id 9 gate is visible in the body.

name: Party_ApplyFontsToAllMembers
summary: Unconditional variant of the font refresh: calls func_0014E3C4 and then re-applies the font/name record of every active party member whose data-table entry has bit 1 set.
evidence: Same loop as 0x001924DC but without the command gate (the only difference), and again the sole operation is the named Text_ApplyFontRecord - so the function refreshes rendered names, it does not recalculate stats.

name: maybe_Party_InitBattleSlots
summary: Writes six consecutive ids 0xBB..0xC0 to the value 0x9C on the hero's record (party index 0), clears the bytes at +0x12E0/+0x12E2 to 0xFF and re-applies the font record.
evidence: The ids 0xBB..0xC0 are set through the unnamed func_00190270(member, id, value), so whether they are battle-command slots, item slots or something else still cannot be shown; the only new detail is that +0x12E0/+0x12E2 are cleared too.

name: Party_UpdateAllMemberRecords
summary: Per-frame pass over the 0x1F party member records at the base of the game work (stride 0x4BB*4 = 0x12EC): re-applies each member's font record, dispatches the member's virtual update with its field at +0xEC and clamps +0x1A between +0x16 and +0xEE; when the current actor changes it restarts the 300-frame timer at work+0x2FB18.
evidence: The loop stride 0x4BB*4 is exactly the party-member record stride used by Party_ApplyFontsOnCommand and Party_ValidateEquipmentNames, and the callee is the named Text_ApplyFontRecord - so this is the member table, not an effect node table. 31 slots also matches the maximum party size.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_CreateSubObject
signature: void* Ui_SakusenWindow_CreateSubObject(void* slot, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Creates and registers the 0x200-byte sub-object of the tactics (sakusen) window: allocates from the UI heap, constructs it with the sakusen sub-object ctor, registers it through Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable, stores it in the slot and clears the slot's ready byte at +0x94.
evidence: The ctor callee is now named maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_SubObjectCtor and the registration helper Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable, so the owning class is the battle-tactics window; the old generic 'Ui_CreateSubObject' hid that.

name: maybe_Text_UpdateStyleParams
summary: Copies the 16 style words cached at self+0x8668..+0x86A4 into a local block and passes them to func_0018CC14 and then func_00613F14, i.e. it rebuilds the text object's style parameters from its cached copy.
evidence: The second callee 0x0018CC14 is currently named maybe_Text_ThrowError and marked non-returning, yet the body calls 0x00613F14 afterwards - that name is very likely wrong (it behaves like a format/convert helper), so this function's exact effect cannot be stated either. Flagged for a follow-up on 0x0018CC14.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_SetRecordHandle
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_SetRecordHandle(UiMessageWindow* self, unsigned int record_handle, unsigned char flag)
summary: Stores the flag byte at self+0x500, resolves the tagged record component selected by the window state (+0x388 picks the +0x60 state value 2 or 3) and copies the subject/speaker string into the window's text buffer at +0x4A4.
evidence: Its vtable sibling 0x0032BD88 has the same body for its own window class (self+0x2D4) and was named Ui_DiveStartWindow_SetRecordHandle by another pass, so the 'set record handle plus copy name' reading is shared; it stays vtable-only, hence 0.50.

name: Gfx_ObjectDesc_Init
signature: GfxObjectDesc* Gfx_ObjectDesc_Init(GfxObjectDesc* self, u32 kind, u32 id, const char* name, u8 mode, u32 flags)
summary: Base initialiser for every named game object descriptor: installs the descriptor vtable pair (0x00193E24/0x00193E28), copies up to 15 bytes of the asset name into the inline buffer at +8, NUL-terminates it and stores kind, id, mode and flags.
evidence: All HUD/NPC/field object constructors route through it (Gfx_ObjectDesc_Ctor4 -> this, and Gfx_ObjectDesc_Ctor4 has 16 named callers such as Field_NpcAction_CtorMoveState and Field_EnemyAiBehavior_Ctor), which makes the 'named object descriptor' role - name buffer at +8, kind word at +0x18 - solid rather than inferred.

name: Field_NpcAction_CtorMoveState
signature: void* Field_NpcAction_CtorMoveState(void* obj, void* owner, void* params, const char* name, u32 mode)
summary: Constructor of the 'moveSt' field-NPC action object (0x34 bytes, vtable 0x0075EDE0): runs the shared descriptor ctor, clears the action byte +0xB and the word at +0xC, and installs the vtable.
evidence: Its three call sites all pass the script name 'moveSt' (s_moveSt at 0x0017A6D8 / 0x0017ABE4 / 0x0017813C) together with a freshly allocated 0x34-byte block, so this is a class constructor, not a 'set idle params' mutator; the old name described the caller's intent, not the callee.

name: Field_NpcAction_CtorAppear
signature: void* Field_NpcAction_CtorAppear(void* obj, void* owner, void* params, const char* name, u32 mode)
summary: Constructor of the 'appear' field-NPC action object (0x2C bytes): runs the shared descriptor ctor and installs vtable 0x00759F10.
evidence: The only call site (Field_SetupNpcActionScript, 0x00177864) allocates 0x2C bytes and passes the script name 'appear' (s_appear at 0x00177D24), next to the sibling constructors for 'disappear', 'notice' and 'moveSt' - so this is the appear-action class ctor.

name: Field_NpcAction_CtorNotice
signature: void* Field_NpcAction_CtorNotice(void* obj, void* owner, void* params, const char* name, u32 mode)
summary: Constructor of the 'notice' field-NPC action object (0x54 bytes, vtable 0x00759F44): sets the two timers 0.4/0.8 at +0xC/+0xD, the two vectors from 0x007E7030/0x007E7000, clears +0x14 and +0x51 and sets +0x52 = 7.
evidence: Its only caller allocates 0x54 bytes and passes 'notice' (s_notice at 0x00177D38) in the same table-driven block that builds the appear/disappear/moveSt actions; the defaults match a timed notice/popup action, so the class is now identified.

name: Field_NpcAction_CtorGesture
signature: void* Field_NpcAction_CtorGesture(void* obj, void* owner, void* params, const char* name, u32 mode)
summary: Constructor of the 'gesture' field-NPC action object (vtable 0x0075BB34): runs the shared descriptor ctor and stores 0.5 at +0x2C.
evidence: Its only caller Field_NpcPlayGesture (0x00179D7C) passes the script name 'gesture' (s_gesture at 0x0017A090) with a pre-allocated block; the old 'register talk-party layout' name described neither the caller intent nor the body.

name: Field_NpcAction_CtorDisappear
signature: void* Field_NpcAction_CtorDisappear(void* obj, void* owner, void* params, const char* name, u32 mode)
summary: Constructor of the 'disappear' field-NPC action object (0x2C bytes): runs the shared descriptor ctor and installs vtable 0x0075ED78.
evidence: The only call site (Field_SetupNpcActionScript) allocates 0x2C bytes and passes 'disappear' (s_disappear at 0x00177D2C); the vtable 0x0075ED78 sits directly below the moveSt (0x75EDE0) and movePa (0x75EDAC) vtables, confirming the sibling class ladder.

name: Field_NpcAction_CtorMoveParam
signature: void* Field_NpcAction_CtorMoveParam(void* obj, void* owner, void* params, const char* name, u32 mode)
summary: Constructor of the 'movePa' field-NPC action object (0x44 bytes, vtable 0x0075EDAC): clears +0xB and +0xC, copies the three-float vector from 0x007E7000 to +0xD..+0xF and stores 2.0 at +0x10.
evidence: Its only caller (Field_NpcApplyAction, 0x0017A8AC) allocates 0x44 bytes and passes 'movePa' (s_movePa at 0x0017ABF0) - a move-parameter action, sibling of the 'moveSt' ctor at 0x002B2F40.

name: Field_EnemyAiBehavior_Ctor
signature: void* Field_EnemyAiBehavior_Ctor(void* obj, void* owner, void* params, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Constructor of one enemy-AI behaviour object (100 bytes, vtable 0x0076487C): runs the shared descriptor ctor and fills the default parameter block, including the duplicated vector triples at +0x34..+0x40.
evidence: Its only caller is the named Field_EnemyAi_CreateBehavior (0x006D5CB0), which allocates 100 bytes per behaviour slot and destroys the object again when registration fails - so it is an enemy-AI component, not a generic monster behaviour.

name: Field_NpcAction_CtorOpeJo
signature: void* Field_NpcAction_CtorOpeJo(void* obj, void* owner, void* params, const char* name, u32 mode)
summary: Constructor of the 'opeJo' field-NPC action object (0x3C bytes, vtable 0x0076A4AC): runs the shared descriptor ctor, clears the word at +0x2C and installs the vtable.
evidence: Its only caller Field_ApplyNpcActionState (0x00179398) allocates 0x3C bytes and passes the script name 'opeJo' (s_opeJo at 0x00179704); the old name was structurally right but unnamed, the new one records the action the game asks for.

name: maybe_Anim_ObjectBaseCtor
summary: Shared base constructor for the animation-curve objects: runs the shared descriptor ctor and stores the same default word at three fields; the callers then overwrite the vtable with their own class.
evidence: The two callers (maybe_Anim_ClipSlot_SetEight 0x002EBDD8 and maybe_Anim_ClipSlot_SetTwo 0x002EBEFC) themselves only have maybe_ names, so the 'animation curve object base' reading is still inherited rather than proven.

name: maybe_Ui_WindowResource_Reset
summary: Rebuilds a small resource holder: when the dirty byte at +4 is set it releases the three cached objects (+0x8, +0xC, +0x10), then creates a 200-byte curve animator, a 0x80-byte and a 0x84-byte animator (only the 0x80 one when the argument is non-zero), hands the 200-byte object to Field_InitSceneObjects with vtable 0x00782234 and re-sets the dirty byte.
evidence: Ghidra removed several blocks (0x00293880..0x002938BC), and the callees that would identify the owner (0x001A366C, maybe_Ui_FadeAnimator_InitCurveA/B) are themselves maybe_-level; the new detail is the three-object triple and the Field_InitSceneObjects hand-off, which does not fit a 'window resource' cleanly.

name: maybe_Battle_PopupPool_Init
signature: void maybe_Battle_PopupPool_Init(int self, unsigned int owner, unsigned int owner2)
summary: Initialises a popup pool: stores the owner, allocates two 8-byte owner handles with the pool vtable, a 0x14-byte pool header and 16 entries of 0x34 bytes (plus sentinel), hands each entry to the entry initialiser (0x0058E264) and clears them; the mirror function 0x002E6428 frees entries by bitmask.
evidence: The only caller is 0x0019CD50 (currently named Field_InitSceneObjects), so 'battle' is doubtful - the same pool serves the field scene that owns it. The pool structure itself (16 x 0x34 entries, sprite sub-pool, bitmask release) is confirmed by the entry initialiser named Battle_PopupPool_InitEntry.

name: maybe_Field_TextObject_Ctor
summary: One-shot constructor of a 0x37C-byte text/effect object: lazily allocates the backing block through 0x0011FE8C/0x0011CFAC, zeroes it, installs the vtable, sets the 0xFF/0 defaults and constructs the eight 8-byte sub-records at +0x2C.
evidence: Its only caller is 0x0019CD50 (Field_InitSceneObjects), which places it in the scene's object set; nothing in the body says 'text', so the class name remains an inheritance from the previous pass.

name: Field_SceneObjectCtor_vt1D582C
summary: Constructor stub of a field scene object: base-initialises through 0x004712D0, installs vtable 0x001D582C, copies the 3-float transform pair from 0x001D5830, sets the class/state bytes (5, 5, 2, 1) and default-constructs the children at +0x54.
evidence: The caller 0x0019CD50 (Field_InitSceneObjects) allocates the object, calls this and stores it, which is the ctor contract; the name only claims the vtable, not a gameplay class, so it can be dropped to non-maybe.

name: Field_SceneObjectCtor_vt21066C
summary: Constructor stub of a second field scene-object class: base-initialises through 0x004712D0, installs the vtable at 0x0021066C, clears +0x10 and default-constructs five 0x40-byte children at +0x14.
evidence: Same allocation/construction pattern and the same caller (Field_InitSceneObjects) as its two siblings, and the installed vtable is visible in the body - the only unproven part is which gameplay object this class represents, which the name does not claim.

name: Field_SceneObjectCtor_vt23EC5C
summary: Constructor stub of a third field scene-object class: base-initialises through 0x004712D0, installs vtable 0x0023EC5C, seeds the two -0x800 position sentinels and default-constructs twelve 4-byte children at +0x1C.
evidence: Caller Field_InitSceneObjects and the installed vtable are both visible; the twelve 4-byte children and the two sentinels are the only content, so the vtable-based name is as much as the evidence supports.

name: Field_SceneSubObject_Ctor
signature: void Field_SceneSubObject_Ctor(SceneSubObject* self, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Constructor of the 0x9D4-byte scene sub-object that Field_InitSceneObjects attaches at self+0x6C: builds its empty intrusive lists, fills the -1000.0 position sentinels, resets the 0xFF slot bytes and default-constructs the two 0x38-byte entries at +0x8F4.
evidence: The caller Field_InitSceneObjects (0x0019CD50) allocates exactly 0x9D4 bytes, calls this and stores the result at self+0x6C, which is the ctor contract; the name still does not claim which gameplay object it is.

name: Ui_ListWindow_InitDataObjects
summary: Creates the three data objects of a list window from the allocator word at params+4 - the list-entry object (0x30), the row-data object (0x30) and the child-window list (0x38) - stores them at +0x14, +0x10 and +0xC and dispatches the selected one's init virtual.
evidence: The three callees are now named (maybe_Ui_ListEntryObject_Ctor, maybe_Ui_ListRowData_Ctor, maybe_Ui_ChildWindowList_Init), so these are the list window's data objects, not generic children of a 'composite window'.

name: maybe_Ui_InitColor
summary: Fills six colour components (color+8..+0x1C) from a 6-word block produced by 0x00113590; Ghidra dropped the source argument, so the visible body only shows the copy half of the operation.
evidence: 0x00113590 is still unnamed and the parameter list was truncated, so neither the direction (palette -> colour or colour -> palette) nor the owning structure can be proven.

name: maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_Ctor
signature: int maybe_Ui_CompositeWindow_Ctor(unsigned int parent, int params)
summary: Constructor of a window that embeds a composite sub-object: creates the outer object through 0x004712D0 with vtable 0x00761E58, constructs the sub-object at +4 with maybe_Ui_CompositeWindowCtor and initialises its default colour/fade fields (+0x114..+0x140).
evidence: The embedded sub-object's ctor carries the 'CompositeWindow' name, so the outer class is something else that hosts one; without a vtable or string identifying the outer class the name keeps the previous wording.

name: Ui_EquipRow_Activate
summary: Activates one equipment row: for a party slot (< 0x1F) it removes the item at the row's slot with maybe_Member_RemoveItemAtSlot, notifies the item table at work+0x24ACC, pushes the row pane and plays the confirm animation (3 or 2 by the member's f_14); for the pseudo-slot 0x1F it toggles the bag count of the row's item and plays animation 0x10.
evidence: The named callee maybe_Member_RemoveItemAtSlot (established: remove the item from a member slot) and the item-table notification show this mutates state; the old 'UpdateEquipMark' described a redraw. Its vtable 0x0076A318 also holds the equip-row compare/curse updaters, which fits a row action.

name: maybe_Ui_FieldMessageWindow_InitB
summary: Place-dependent window open: if the current place id is 1 it sets menu mode 1, pushes the first pane descriptor and plays steps 0x0F/0x11; otherwise it pushes the alternate descriptor, plays 0x0F/0x10 and, when the record lookup succeeds, hands self+0x14 to the panel and resets/pushes it.
evidence: The branch condition is the named maybe_Field_GetCurrentPlaceId and the sibling call maybe_Ui_Menu_SetMode(app+0x48,1) shows a menu-mode switch, but the class is still only identified by the previous pass - keep maybe_.

name: Ui_EquipmentWindow_OpenDetailEx
signature: void Ui_EquipmentWindow_OpenDetailEx(UiEquipmentWindow* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Opens the item-detail pane of the equipment window with the alternate animation descriptor (0x00729ACC+0x60/+0x64) and the item list at arg2+0x11C; unlike Ui_EquipmentWindow_OpenDetail it neither clears +0x1BC nor dispatches the callback.
evidence: Its sibling Ui_EquipmentWindow_OpenDetail (0x0019AD74) is named and has the identical shape with descriptor +0x58; this variant differs only by the descriptor and by omitting the two trailing calls, so the 'Ex' reading is confirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_TitleWindow_SetAnimFrame
signature: void maybe_Ui_TitleWindow_SetAnimFrame(UiTitleWindow* self, unsigned int frame, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int arg4)
summary: Plays frame-script step 0x36 on the window, binds the detail widget at owner+0x1084 to owner+0x111C and pushes the pane descriptor at 0x00729A7C+0x48. It is the 'open' member of the push-pane/step family whose close counterparts are 0x00617DD4 and 0x003D66C4.
evidence: The step player 0x00617D7C is still unnamed, so 'set animation frame' remains a guess about what 0x36 means; the pane push and the descriptor at +0x48 are visible, hence the family relationship noted in the summary.

name: Ui_EquipmentWindow_CloseAlt
summary: Secondary close of the equipment window: pushes the closing pane descriptor (0x00729A7C+0x38), plays frame-script step 0x19 and releases the owner window through 0x0019AD70.
evidence: It shares vtable 0x0076A318 with Ui_EquipmentWindow_HandleInput (0x00617FB0) and the equip-row updaters, and its body is the same close sequence as 0x00617DD4 ('dHL') with a different descriptor - so 'DiveForm_DeleteB' named the wrong class and the wrong operation.

name: Ui_EquipmentWindow_RefreshDetail
summary: Rebuilds the equipment window's detail side: resolves the highlighted item through Ui_EquipmentWindow_FindItemIndex, reads its name, walks the two intrusive lists (+0xEC0/+0x9EC), plays the list-move sound helpers and marks the detail pane's dirty flags (+0x1C/+0x1D/+0x18) so it redraws.
evidence: Both entry points are named (Ui_EquipmentWindow_Update and 0x0019903C) and the callees now include Ui_EquipmentWindow_FindItemIndex plus func_0066C724 for the name length, so the detail-refresh role is supported by more than the field writes.

name: maybe_Ui_TwoPageListWindow_Init
signature: void maybe_Ui_TwoPageListWindow_Init(UiWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Initialises a two-page text list: resets the layout part at +0x4C, fills two rows from the first two ids of the static table at 0x00729B3C and clamps the selection to the last row.
evidence: The table at 0x00729B3C holds {0x0A,0x0F} for this initial page, {0x0A,0x0B,0x0E,0x0F} for page 0 and {0x0A..0x0F} for page 1, i.e. 2/4/5 rows; the previous 'TwoChoiceDialog' (two entries everywhere) was wrong about the page sizes.

name: maybe_Ui_TwoPageListWindow_SetPage
summary: Switches the two-page list: page 0 restarts the layout part at +0x9C with four ids, any other page restarts +0xEC with five ids, and each branch clamps the selection to its last row.
evidence: Same static id table (0x00729B3C) as the initialiser, with four ids for page 0 and five for page 1 - not the 'four vs five of a two-choice dialog' the previous name implied.

name: Ui_ItemListCore_ApplyMode
summary: Re-applies the stored item-list mode: re-initialises the list iterator at self+0x17 with the mode byte at self[0x1F] and, when the flag at self[0x16] is set, notifies the owning widget through vtable slot +0x5C.
evidence: The callee is now the named maybe_ItemList_Iterator_Init, so the stored mode byte really is an iterator mode; callers (Ui_EquipmentWindow_Confirm/Update, 0x0019A514, 0x001E9FE8/0x001EAE88) all re-enter the list after changing selection or mode.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithCutscene
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithCutscene(UiMessageWindow* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Closes a message window that owns a cutscene: ends the cutscene object at +0x70 (Cutscene_Close), sends cutscene commands 1 and 2, parks the child group 1 of the widget at +0x54 and notifies the UI core.
evidence: All three leads are named callees (Cutscene_Close, Event_OnCutSceneCommand, Ui_Widget_DispatchToGroupedChildren) and no pager object is touched, so the previous 'CloseWithPager' named the wrong thing.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithScene
signature: void Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithScene(UiMessageWindow* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Closes a message window that owns a sub-scene: releases the scene object at +0x5C (maybe_Gfx_Scene_Release), clears the choice handler at core+0x14 and parks the child group 1 of the widget at +0x54.
evidence: The f_5C object is released with maybe_Gfx_Scene_Release, which contradicts the previous 'choice widget' reading of that field; the choice-handler reset is the separate core+0x14+0xC virtual.

name: maybe_Ui_OverlaySlot_SetStateByte
summary: Stores the value byte into the overlay slot's f_C1C and then dispatches part group 8 with mode 0 on the game work's widget holder (work+0x54), i.e. stores the state and refreshes the overlay group.
evidence: Its twin at 0x0023AE04 has the identical body with the two arguments swapped, so the old pair of names ('release parts and store byte' vs 'store byte and release parts') described one operation twice; group 8 is a part mask, not a release.

name: maybe_Ui_OverlaySlot_SetStateByteB
summary: Twin of 0x0023A080 with the arguments in (slot, value) order: writes f_C1C and dispatches part group 8 with mode 0.
evidence: Byte-for-byte the same operation as its sibling apart from argument order; only one of the two can be reached from a given vtable slot, and neither has a named caller, so it keeps maybe_ and a B suffix.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_AssignEntryOrder
summary: Re-numbers the overlay entries: walks the 0xC-byte entries from index 1, writes a running counter into word +0x8A of each and calls 0x003E7110(element, index); the anchor entry is given order 0.
evidence: The decompiler lost registers (unaff_r* / overlapping instructions at 0x00239EFC), so the anchor handling and the exact call arguments are still guesses; no named caller or callee was found.

name: BattleActor_ShowActionEffect
summary: Shows one of the battle actor's action-effect sprites from a 6-byte argument record (kind, two sprite params, u16 id): chooses the sprite kind, copies the params into the sprite fields, resolves the message text (instant or delayed) and sets the actor state byte to 0x0E.
evidence: The named caller Battle_SetActorEffectId (0x00148F08) passes {slot, 0xFF, 0xFF} records and validates the per-kind id ranges before calling, which pins this as the action-effect slot display; the sibling maybe_BattleActor_ShowStateEffect (0x0019EE60) covers the state effects.

name: Ui_TrainingWindow_UpdateInput
summary: Per-frame update of the training window: when the page-cursor object is at rest it samples the pad cursor, the scene colour and the BGM id, then advances the window's frame script to the moved/confirmed/cancelled step (0x0C/0x0D/0x0E) and commits the pending BGM.
evidence: Its class siblings are named (Ui_TrainingWindow_InitPanes 0x00261BAC and maybe_Ui_FrameScript_Update 0x00261F40) and the body's only work is the pad/BGM sampling plus the frame-script step dispatch, so the update-input role is confirmed.

name: BattleActor_ShowFixedEffect
summary: Fixed-id variant of the battle action effect: always uses effect id 0x406, sprite kind 7 and actor state 0x0F, copies the 0x406 id into the local sound struct, asks the item/effect manager for 0x406 and plays the text by id.
evidence: Its callers are named (Battle_SetActorEffectId path and 0x004CCB30), and the hard-coded 0x406 appears four times in the body together with sprite kind 7 - the 'fixed effect' reading is literal, not structural.

name: SceneFlow_TryCommitTransition
summary: One-shot commit of a pending scene transition: while nothing is loading (sound player idle, no pending pack data, loading screen neither active nor finished) it stamps the loading-screen colour from +0x3C/+0x3D, clears the global render flag, stops the sound player and marks byte +6 = 1 as committed; returns 1 either way.
evidence: Named callees Pack_GetManager, Ui_LoadingScreen_IsActive/IsFinished, Ui_LoadingScreen colour setter and Sound_GetPlayer show this is the transition commit gate, not a preload; the 'Ui_SceneFlow' owner prefix is kept because the caller is UI scene flow code.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_CommitScene
summary: Commits the prepared scene: initialises the scene sprite set and the scene object, calls the event callbacks, loads the world map models and advances the flow counter at +0x1D while storing the incoming halfword at +0x20.
evidence: The readable body uses unaff_r4/unaff_r5 (arguments lost) and in_s16, so per the project's decompilation-damage rule the name stays maybe_ and confidence at 0.30; the visible callees (Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_Init, Gfx_Scene_Init, Ui_SceneFlow_LoadWorldMapModels) do, however, contradict the previous 'message window state machine' name.

name: Gfx_CreateMultiSpriteEffect
summary: Builds the eight-sprite layered effect used for glows/shadows around an actor: takes the shape descriptor, creates the colour animator, then for i = 0..7 resolves the frame id and per-sprite transform and adds a child sprite at self+0x298+i*0x48 with flags 0xFFE.
evidence: The loop and callees are now named (Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, Gfx_CreateFColAnimator, Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild, Gfx_SpriteParts_SetFlag239), which confirms the eight-child construction and the colour animator.

name: Gfx_CreateMultiSpriteEffectB
summary: Second copy of the eight-sprite layered effect builder: same colour animator, same i = 0..7 child loop into self+0x298+i*0x48, only the constant addresses differ.
evidence: The body is identical to 0x001A3CA4 (template copy), so the previous 'RingSpriteEffect' name invented a difference that the code does not have; the B suffix records that it is a duplicate.
